scope: Finite ordered-pair packing and arithmetic imply total heavy excess <=k whenever the complement of Y has at most 2k+1 points. The final theorem proves the exact 997 inequality under n<=3*|Y|+1, including Y of size0 or1 via checked SmallWindow. The unrestricted 997 inequality remains open.
math_audit: Distinct targets with intersection size at most one have disjoint sets of ordered pairs of distinct points.
For heavy targets, all ordered pairs lie in the complement of Y, giving sum d_i(d_i-1)<=q(q-1).
For every natural d,k, d(d-1)>=(4k+2)*max(d-k-1,0). Above the truncation point the difference factors as (d-2k-1)(d-2k-2), nonnegative for integral d.
q<=2k+1 yields q(q-1)<=(4k+2)k; positive-factor cancellation bounds the total excess by k.
The final statement adds only n<=3*Y.card+1 to the posted hypotheses; the same checked refundGates predicate is used and is definitionally equal to the posted predicate.
No lower bound on target sizes, no distinctness assumption beyond pairwise intersection at most one, and no validity assumption on circuit references was added.
